CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  CITY ARTS & CULTURAL EVENTS COMMITTEE AGENDA
  Regular Meeting
  Wednesday, June 19, 2019 7:00 P.M.
  Alhambra City Hall
  111 South First Street, Alhambra, 91801
  Conference Room A
  Homewood Suites by Hilton Seattle-Tacoma Airport
  6955 Fort Dent Way, Tukwila, WA 98188

  I.  ROLL CALL
  Brian Canseco-Chan, President (Teleconferencing from Homewood Suites by Hilton Seattle-Tacoma Airport, WA)
  Karsen Luthi, Vice President
  Michael Lawrence
  Camille Rutkowski
  Aide Zeller

 II.  FLAG SALUTE

III.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF THE MAY 15, 2019 REGULAR MEETING

IV.  STAFF REPORT

 V.  PUBLIC COMMUNICATION
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments must pertain to
  the business of the Alhambra City Arts and Cultural Events Committee. Public comments
  pertaining to the Committee’s business are welcome. Kindly limit all oral communications to
  five (5) minutes. Please complete the blue speaker card prior to the meeting and submit it to the
  Committee Secretary.

VI.  COMMITTEE COMMUNICATION
  Discussion from the Committee Members of any item(s) not specified on the agenda. Items
  discussed must pertain to the business of the Alhambra City Arts and Cultural Events.

VII.  ADJOURNMENT
  Discussion from the Committee Members of any item(s) not specified on the agenda. Items
  discussed must pertain to the business of the Alhambra City Arts and Cultural Events.

Copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each type of business described herein above are on file in
the office of Parks & Recreation, Alhambra City Hall, 111 S. First Street, Alhambra, and are available for public inspection
during office hours: 8:00. A.M. to 5:00 P.M. Monday through Friday. Should any person have a question concerning any of
the above agenda items prior to the meeting described herein, please contact the Committee Secretary either in person or in
the Parks & Recreation department located at City Hall or call (626) 570-5044 during regular business hours.
 Approved by the  May 15, 2019
City Arts and Cultural Events Committee  Action Item III
  APPROVED

  MINUTES
  ALHAMBRA CITY ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS COMMITTEE
  Wednesday, April 17, 2019, 7:00 P.M.

The regular meeting of the City Arts and Cultural Events Committee was called to order at 7:17
P.M. on April 17, 2019 at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street Alhambra, Conference
Room A.

ROLL CALL
Committee Members Present: Luthi, Canseco Chan, Lawrence, Rutkowski, and Zeller
Committee Members Absent: None; all committee members were present.
Also attending: Director Michael Macias, Deputy Director Brie Houghton, and Clerical Assistant
II Kelsey Rivadeneyra

ELECTION OF OFFICERS FOR 2019/2020 TERM
President Brian Canseco Chan
Vice President Karsen Luthi

APPROVAL OF MINUTES
Committee Member Luthi moved to approve the minutes of the September 19, 2018 C.A.C.E
meeting were approved as written.

POWERPOINT PRESENTATION OF THE HISTORY OF PUBLIC ART FUND BY
COMMITTEE MEMBER MICHAEL LAWRENCE

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION
Greg Miller inquired what is the total cost of a Rose Parade float built by volunteers, and
Director Macias responded that it would cost a quarter of a million dollars. Miller questioned
why the Chamber of Commerce does not get funding from their members to sponsor the annual
City of Alhambra Rose Parade float? Miller would like to see public art such as statues displayed
throughout the City.

Oscar Omaro supports the idea of restoring the broken neon “Alhambra” signs located at the
City’s borders. He asked where the main source of revenue for public art comes from, and
Director Macias responded that a .5% percentage of the building’s value comes back to the Art
Fund from new residential and commercial construction. Funds are held in accounts until City
Council chooses to allocate the money. Omaro said that speaking as a former C.A.C.E. member,
he felt that there was a resistance within the commission and that there was no thinking outside
the box. He would like to see the art commission explore more creative avenues for the public art
fund instead of the Rose Parade Float.
 Lola Armendariz would like to see funds spent on restorations of famous Alhambra landmarks
such as the clock on Main Street and signage. Armendariz asked who decides what type of
artwork? Deputy Director Houghton responded, if it’s going to be done by the developer, the
developer has to present it to the C.A.C.E. committee who then recommends it to the Planning
Commission for approval. C.A.C.E. reviews the art whether it represents Alhambra or if it’s
appropriate. The money comes into the art fund when the developer chooses not to do an art
feature, and they pay a percentage into the art fund. If the developer chooses to build art into
their development, they do not pay into the art fund but it needs to go through the approval
process.

Committee member Lawrence asked if there was any sort of screening done on the art and if
C.A.C.E. does any actual research on the value of the art before installation.

Deputy Director Houghton replied that it hasn’t happened since her leading the committee and
the process has only been explained to her. From her experience she has noticed that developers
pay the fee instead of installing art.

Armendariz expressed that in her many years of attending planning commissions, she has not
seen a developer come forward for an art install.

Miller asked what kind of cultural events the committee assists with and Deputy Director
Houghton explained that C.A.CE. is currently working together with the upcoming Latino
Heritage Festival to have a chalk art festival as an art component.

Miller would like to see a performing arts theatre in Alhambra since the lizard mosaic theatre is
no longer on Main Street.

Deputy Director Houghton expressed that since the C.A.C.E. committee came under the Parks
and Recreation Department a year ago, the focus is to bring art in as an element to community
events. It is an advisory committee that discusses how to bring culture and art into the City.
Approval comes from the Planning Commission and City Council after recommendation from
C.A.C.E.

Armendariz would like to see in the future, one big event for various cultures within the
community such as the past “Hi Neighbor Parade”. She recommends holding events on Second
Street instead of in the parks so that it can generate revenue for local businesses on Main Street
and the street can be closed off.

COMMITTEE COMMUNICATION
Luthi agrees that the broken neon “Alhambra” border signs need to be taken care of and suggests
that the Downtown Alhambra Business Association could get involved and assist.

Lawrence wants the C.A.C.E. committee to take care of the restoration and if needed, reach out
to the Downtown Alhambra Business Association for assistance. He has a rough estimate from a
local vendor and wants to know as a committee how they can move forward with the restoration
of the broken neon “Alhambra” border signs.
 On a motion of Lawrence with a second by Zeller, all are in favor to have the City conduct
research on the logistics of the neon “Alhambra” border signs restoration.

Canseco-Chan would like to add that there are other historic landmarks within the City that
needs attention or utility boxes that could benefit from restoration and beautification.

ADJOURNMENT
Committee Member Canseco Chan moved to adjourn the City Arts and Cultural Events Committee
Meeting. Seconded by Committee Member Luthi, the meeting was adjourned at 8:15 p.m.
 Approved by the  May 15, 2019
City Arts and Cultural Events Committee  Action Item II
  APPROVED

  MINUTES
  SPECIAL MEETING
  ALHAMBRA CITY ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS COMMITTEE
  Wednesday, April 17, 2019, 7:00 P.M.

The special meeting of the City Arts and Cultural Events Committee was called to order at 7:03
P.M. on April 17, 2019 at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street Alhambra, Conference
Room A.

ROLL CALL
Committee Members Present: Luthi, Canseco Chan, Lawrence, Rutkowski, and Zeller
Committee Members Absent: None; all committee members were present.
Also attending: Director Michael Macias, Deputy Director Brie Houghton, and Clerical Assistant
II Kelsey Rivadeneyra

SPECIAL EVENTS UPDATE
Director Macias presented three City of Alhambra 2020 Rose Parade float renderings, created by
the Phoenix Decorating Company, to the committee for review. On the motion of Canseco-Chan
with a second by Rutkowski, the committee chose a rendering with a train theme for
recommendation to the City Council. Committee member Lawrence abstained from voting.

ADJOURNMENT
On the motion of Luthi with a second by Canseco-Chan, the meeting adjourned at 7:16 P.M.
 Unofficial until adopted by the  June 19, 2019
City Arts and Cultural Events Committee  Action Item III
  APPROVE

  MINUTES
  ALHAMBRA CITY ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS COMMITTEE
  Wednesday, May 15, 2019 7:00 P.M.

The regular meeting of the City Arts and Cultural Events Committee was called to order at 7:03
P.M. on Wednesday May 15, 2019 at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street Alhambra,
Conference Room A.

ROLL CALL
Committee Members Present: Canseco Chan, Luthi, Lawrence, Rutkowski, and Zeller.
Committee Members Absent: None
Also attending: Director Michael Macias and Clerical Assistant II Kelsey Rivadeneyra.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF THE APRIL 17, 2019 SPECIAL MEETING
On the motion of Vice President Luthi with a second by Lawrence, the minutes of the April 17,
2019 Special Meeting were unanimously approved as written.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF THE APRIL 17, 2019 REGULAR MEETING
On the motion of Committee Member Rutkowski with a second by Zeller, the minutes of the
April 17, 2019 Regular Meeting were unanimously approved as written.

STAFF REPORT
Director Macias informed the committee that the City is looking for artists to exhibit their art
pieces in the Alhambra City Hall lobby for the 2020 year. Committee members are encouraged
to find and recommend possible artists at upcoming C.A.CE. meetings.

Next item discussed by Director Macias was to inform how staff conducted research and came
up with a general cost for the restoration of the Alhambra neon city entry and exits signs. The
general cost for new neon lettering on both sides, new neon transformers, sand primer, matching
paint, and new “Alhambra” and “Come Again Soon” script in white was estimated at $2,879 per
sign and an estimated total of $8,637 without electrical work. Staff anticipates electrical work
required as well to complete the restoration. The City Arts and Cultural Events Committee
directed Director Macias to prepare a staff report and recommend to Alhambra City Council, a
request to go out to bid for an appropriation of funds from the Art in Public Places account to
undertake action for the Alhambra neon sign project. Committee member Lawrence requested
research be done on the origin of the neon city entry and exit signs.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION
None

COMMITTEE COMMUNICATION
 Committee member Lawrence presented a PowerPoint showing examples of public art in
neighboring cities, across the country, and abroad. Lawrence would like to have the committee
go on a Los Angeles art tour with the community to find inspiration for permanent public art to
display in the City of Alhambra. Macias informed the committee that he will look into an art
excursion and speak with Gail McKinney from the Joslyn Senior Center.

Vice President Luthi reminded the City Arts and Cultural Events Committee that the Chalk Art
Festival in conjunction with the Latino Heritage Festival will take place on September 15, 2019.
Artist applications are available on the website and Luthi hopes that there will be enough
applicants to bring for review at the July City Arts and Cultural Events Committee meeting.

Committee members stated which member of the City Council appointed them for the City Arts
and Cultural Events Committee. City Council Member Jeffrey Maloney appointed Karsen Luthi,
City Council Member Katherine Lee appointed Michael Lawrence, City Council Member David
Mejia appointed Camille Rutkowski, Mayor Adele Andrade-Stradler appointed Aide Zeller, and
City Council Member Ross Maza appointed Brian Canseco-Chan.

ADJOURNMENT
Committee Member Canseco Chan moved to adjourn the City Arts and Cultural Events Committee
Meeting. Seconded by Committee Member Luthi, the meeting was adjourned at 7:33 P.M.
